title: Is Zapier GDPR Compliant? What to Check Before Buying
summary: Zapier GDPR compliance covers specific data handling features across pricing plans. Determine whether the protections meet your regulatory requirements.
body_markdown:
## When Activepieces fits a stricter residency requirement


When your requirement is that workflow data stay in a region or a network you choose, Activepieces fits.


> What gets fined is decisions you make about what to collect and why, not a vendor's missing certificate.


It has a managed cloud in an EU or US region, and its SOC 2 programme is in progress, with the penetration test summary, DPA and sub-processor list available on request. It also has a self-hosted option, air-gapped if you need it, that never sends data outside your environment. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


That ranking of residency demands sets the order of the vendor questions below, and the table shows where the two products differ on the controls those questions touch.


Read the Zapier column as what Zapier documents on its own pages, and verify each cell there before relying on it.


Requirement Zapier as documented Activepieces


SOC 2 Type II Check Zapier's trust pages for the current report and scope In progress; pen test summary and DPA on request


SSO/SCIM Check Zapier's plan pages for the tier that includes it SSO and SCIM offered


Custom RBAC Check Zapier's documentation for role granularity Custom RBAC offered


Audit logs Check Zapier's plan pages for availability and retention Audit logs offered


Hosting (EU/US cloud, self-host, air-gap) Check Zapier's documentation for hosting and region options Managed cloud in an EU or US region; self-host; air-gap


The air-gapped self-hosted build is not a cut-down edition: the same six enterprise controls (SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, release management and secret managers) appear in its docs as in the managed cloud's, whether that cloud is pinned to the EU or the US.


Tighter residency therefore does not cost you a control. A listed control is still a claim, so the security documents, not this table, are what you attach to your record.


### Managed cloud in an EU or US region


Activepieces' managed cloud lets you choose an EU or US region up front, which prevents a workflow payload landing in a region your DPA never named. Its SOC 2 programme is in progress, and the penetration test summary, DPA and sub-processor list are available on request.


The answer to "where is this processed" is then a deployment decision you can write into the contract rather than a default you discover later.


Confirm the region applies to workflow data and run logs, not only to the account record.


### Self-host and air-gap


Run Activepieces, whose core is MIT-licensed, on infrastructure you control and the boundary moves from a contract clause to a network edge. An **air-gapped deployment keeps data from leaving your network** at all.


If you are a regulated team, you can use this to keep data in your own environment. That's an architecture, not a certification: it doesn't give you a HIPAA attestation or an ISO certificate, and nothing here claims either.


You also take on patching, backups and uptime, which the managed cloud would otherwise carry.


### Access control and audit logs


Residency says where data sits; access control says who can touch it. Activepieces provides SSO and SCIM in both the managed cloud and the air-gapped build, so joiners and leavers follow your identity provider instead of manual cleanup.


Custom RBAC lets you restrict who can edit a workflow that handles personal data, and audit logs give you the record of who changed what when a regulator or customer asks.


Before you sign, ask each vendor which plan includes each control, what the audit logs record and for how long, and which regions apply to run data.


Activepieces lists Plus at $20 a month and Team at $200 a month on its pricing page, with Ultimate handled through[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) , which means prospective customers cannot evaluate all three tiers without a sales conversation.
